title: Function overloads and implementation signatures
hook: Function overloads let you declare multiple call signatures for one implementation — callers get precise types per arity, while the body uses a wider union. Unlike C# true overloads, TypeScript emits a single JavaScript function.

blocks.text: **Overload signatures** are multiple `function foo(x: string): number` declarations followed by one **implementation** `function foo(x: any): any`. Callers match the best overload; the implementation signature is hidden from external callers. Overloads exist only at **compile time** — emitted JS has one function. Use when **return type or arity** changes meaningfully. For simple optional params, prefer defaults or options objects instead.

entries.plainDefinition: Single function body with compatible wider types.
Multiple call lines in interface for callable types.
entries.example: interface M { (a: string): void; (a: number): void; }

blocks.text: Libraries like `createElement`, `document.querySelector`, and custom factories use overloads for ergonomic APIs. C# compiles each overload to a different CLR signature with name mangling — TypeScript cannot. Interview trap: implementation signature must be compatible with all overloads — often uses `any` or union internally.

blocks.title: When not to overload
blocks.body: Union parameters + type guards often replace overloads with less boilerplate.

blocks.title: Overloading everything
blocks.body: Generics or discriminated unions often replace overload sprawl — easier to maintain.

blocks.text: Overload resolution picks first matching overload in order — order matters. Generic overloads: function identity<T>(x: T): T. Class method overloads use same pattern. Conditional return types sometimes replace overloads (single signature, inferred return). .d.ts files for JS libs use overloads heavily (@types/node).

blocks.title: What gets you rejected
blocks.body: Thinking TS emits multiple functions. Implementation signature visible to callers (it's not externally). Cannot explain overload ordering.

interviewTakeaways: Overloads: multiple declare signatures + one implementation body.
Emitted JS: single function — compile-time only feature.
Implementation must satisfy all overload signatures.
60s: Overloads for call-site precision. One JS function. Narrow in body. C# has real multiple methods. Prefer unions/generics when simpler.
commonPitfalls: Weak: TS creates multiple runtime functions — it does not.
Weak: implementation signature exported to callers — hidden externally.
Strong: Order overloads carefully. Widen implementation. Use unions when overload count explodes.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS has no overload concept — manual typeof checks inside one function mirror TS implementation bodies.
Modern alternative to overloads for some patterns — single signature with inferred return.
